A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAA research, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. All supplied pages were inspected: v1 ends with references, while v2 includes Appendices A–F and a checklist. The retained material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet attack-success measurements, feature-similarity analyses, Grad-CAM visualizations, and component and training-epoch ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds ensemble and defense evaluations, loss and supervision ablations, resource measurements, and feature-based attack comparisons.

M1.justification: The core spatial and adversarial losses and example-generation procedure remain intact. However, v1's explicit multi-witness averaging extension in Equation 7 is removed; v2 presents single-witness updates. Algorithm 1 primarily clarifies existing classifier-head and pseudo-label computations.

E1.justification: Both retain the 1,000-image ImageNet-compatible dataset and untargeted image-classification attacks. v2 extends testing to defended-input scenarios, including randomization, compression, denoising and purification in Table 6. It adds no dataset, application domain or prediction task.

E2.justification: The original alignment and transfer-attack comparators remain. v2 adds FDA and FDA-MI comparisons with and without SAA in Table 11, plus direct unaligned logit ensembles as comparators in Table 5. The defenses in Table 6 are evaluated targets, rather than additional attack baselines.

E3.justification: Sections 3.3–3.4 introduce two- and four-model logit-ensemble protocols and evaluation against 12 defenses using an ensemble of separately aligned surrogates. These substantially expand the evaluation design. The original MI perturbation budget, ten iterations, momentum and one-epoch alignment settings remain unchanged; no changed protocol is stated for the revised Table 3 scores.

E4.justification: v2 adds comparisons of KL/TV/JS/NCE global losses, witness versus surrogate supervision, and hard versus soft local labels, alongside defense testing, computational-cost analysis and target-model Grad-CAM examples. The original component ablation is retained as Table 7, and the unchanged epoch analysis moves to Appendix C.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals or significance tests for its results. v2's checklist cites computational cost to explain the absence of statistical reporting, but introduces no uncertainty estimates or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises ViT-B and Swin-B scores throughout and changes most averages. For example, SSA-DI-TI-MI-SAA average ASR changes from 92.0% to 88.2%, reducing its reported advantage from 5.1 to 2.0 percentage points under the same stated setup. v2 also adds substantial results in Tables 5–6 and 8–11 and Figure 4. Tables 1, 2 and 4 remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 7 narrows the formal update from averaging over a witness-model set to using one witness. Equation 2's pseudo-label rewrite is equivalent once local logits are clarified. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claims about spatial/adversarial alignment and cross-architecture transferability remain essentially unchanged. v2 adds empirical guidance for selecting surrogate and witness models as an explicit contribution in the introduction.

C2.justification: v2 adds model-selection guidance, interpretations supporting the loss and supervision choices, and explicit limitations concerning residual architectural gaps and alignment cost. Appendix F develops a face-forgery misuse scenario and proposed mitigations. These substantially expand v1's interpretation and applicability discussion; the lack-of-theory caveat was already present.

D1.justification: v2 adds detailed loss pseudocode, identifies timm as the model-weight source, and discloses the 1:1 adversarial-to-training-sample ratio. Appendix C reports batch sizes, RTX 3090 hardware, 2,794 MB memory use, and approximately ten hours for SAA versus two for MA. It also points to supplementary code, whose actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The existing related-work discussion and positioning against MA are retained in Appendix A. Additional citations support the defense evaluations, FDA comparison, contrastive-loss ablation and architectural discussion. This extends the literature coverage without substantially redefining the research position.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the original prose are closely preserved. Related Work moves to Appendix A, the epoch discussion moves to Appendix C, and localized methodological explanations and affiliations are revised. New experimental subsections, appendices and a limitations paragraph organize the additions, without extensive rewriting of the retained narrative.

P2.justification: The two-column presentation becomes a single-column NeurIPS layout, substantially changing table sizing, figure placement and text wrapping. v2 adds six tables, Algorithm 1 and Figure 4. Existing displays are retained or relocated, including the unchanged training-epoch Figure 3 in Appendix C.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation and transparency: defended-target evaluations and controlled loss/supervision comparisons address previously untested aspects, while pseudocode and measured resource costs clarify implementation and practical tradeoffs. Table 3 also resolves its MI-result disagreement with Table 2. Missing uncertainty estimates and new FDA prose/table discrepancies remain, but the added diagnostic evidence and reproducibility information provide a substantial net improvement.
